$comment: delta_rules.json — ALL document-independent policy for estimate comparison.
THE GENERAL RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO ENFORCE: nothing here may name a claim,
a carrier, a vehicle, an RO, or a file. If a fix can only be expressed by
naming one of those it is not a fix, it is a patch, and it will not survive
Code contains mechanism; this file contains policy. To change behaviour for
every future comparison, edit this file — never the annotator.
THREE SECTIONS OF THE SOURCE SPEC ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT, because they
already exist elsewhere in this repo and a second copy would drift:
canonical_ops -> data/operationAliases.json is the operation vocabulary.
The spec renamed every key (OP_PRE_SCAN for
PRE_REPAIR_SCAN); opCodeAliases below records the rename
returns 'Workfile' against a CCC stacked label block,
which is the defect that gate was written to fix.
numeric prose -> ai/numericIntegrity.ts already implements R11.
$extractionComment: R19. A missing_operation finding is a claim about the OTHER document, so it
requires having read the other document. The first image-only comparison
recovered no line items; the matcher compared 250 subject lines against an
empty pool and every one came back 'not written on the comparison estimate'.
minParsedRowsForLineVerdicts mirrors the absolute floor in
assessComparisonExtraction — an absolute count, not a ratio, because every
ratio computed from the rows that parsed rises as extraction gets worse.
$totalsVocabularyComment: R22. The totals reader accepts any row carrying letters and a number, which
on an OCR'd supplement made spending categories out of the publisher's
copyright block: 'All Rights Reserved ($0.00, 18 hr @ $0.00/hr)' shipped as
an AMOUNT DELTA finding. Reject list rather than allow list — an allow list
silently drops a real category when a platform renames one, and a dropped
category breaks the reconciliation with no visible symptom.

match.note: CCC underlines its own *-rows; never use underline for match

$rejectMetaTitlesComment: A source may back a finding only if it EVIDENCES the subject, not if it
discusses the subject. 'Tips on Finding OEM Position Statements' and
'How Important Are OEM Position Statements?' are advice about the
existence of position statements; neither IS one. RO 22116 cited the
first of those 11 times as the authority for OEM findings.
Matched case-insensitively against the whole title.
